moments.selftext: BREAKING: 𝕏 wins lawsuit against Australia’s eSafety Commissioner. Elon Musk’s 𝕏 has secured a major victory in Australia’s Federal Court. The eSafety Commissioner argued that 𝕏 should be regulated under two separate online safety systems because the platform offers DMs and encrypted chat, potentially subjecting it to stricter requirements and penalties of up to A$49.5 million. Justice Elizabeth Raper rejected that argument, ruling that 𝕏 cannot be classified as both a “social media service” and a “relevant electronic service.” A major win for 𝕏 against regulatory overreach.

moments.selftext: Clint Eastwood with his first wife, Maggie Johnson, at their home in Los Angeles, 1956. Clint Eastwood was only 23 when he married Maggie Johnson in December 1953. At the time, he was nowhere near the Hollywood icon he would become. Born in San Francisco in 1930, Eastwood had worked a string of ordinary jobs—including as a gas-station attendant, logger, truck driver, and steel-furnace worker—before being drafted into the U.S. Army, where he served as a swimming instructor at Fort Ord. This photograph was taken in 1956, when Eastwood was 26 and still struggling to establish himself as an actor. Universal had signed him to a contract in 1954, but dropped him after roughly a year and a half. He continued taking small roles and odd jobs before landing the part of Rowdy Yates on Rawhide in 1958, the breakthrough that finally put him on the path to stardom. Just eight years later, he would become an international movie star through Sergio Leone’s Dollars trilogy. Looking at the young Eastwood in 1956, it is remarkable to realize that he was still several years away from becoming the instantly recognizable Clint Eastwood of Westerns and crime films. The man who would eventually direct Unforgiven and Million Dollar Baby was, at this point, simply a young actor trying to get noticed in Hollywood.

Novak, best known for playing Ryan Howard on The Office, to a public-domain website. Because the image was now freely available, it ended up being used on all kinds of random products around the world. When Novak eventually discovered what had happened, he reportedly found the situation more amusing than frustrating, saying, “I am too amused to do anything about it.”

moments.selftext: Shocking stat of the day: Estimated annualized interest expense on US federal debt is up to a record $1.38 trillion. This is equivalent to 4.2% of US GDP, the highest percentage since 1997. By comparison, this figure stood at 2.3% in Q4 2020. Annualized interest expense has surged +$900 billion, or nearly +200%, over the last 5 years, rising at an average annual rate of +24%. Meanwhile, in the first 9 months of FY2026, interest expense jumped +$78 billion YoY, to $827 billion, the highest level for this period in history. The cost of servicing US federal debt has never been higher.

moments.title: ELON MUSK ON BUILDING A “STAR MIND” POWERED BY THE SUN “We’ve already built the most powerful AI training clusters in the world. And then what we expect to do by the end of next year is about 10 times more than what we’v
moments.selftext: ELON MUSK ON BUILDING A “STAR MIND” POWERED BY THE SUN “We’ve already built the most powerful AI training clusters in the world. And then what we expect to do by the end of next year is about 10 times more than what we’ve done thus far. This will be very important practice for space AI. And I do think that AI training will continue to be on the ground, but AI inference, the day-to-day use of AI, will be in space. So we’re aiming to get to 10 gigawatts by the end of next year. This is depending on what the value per watt is. If the value per watt is probably going to be $30 to $50, which means if we bring 10 gigawatts of AI online by the end of next year, it will be $300 to $500 billion a year in revenue. Big numbers. And sometimes I wonder, what is our purpose? And it could be that the purpose of humanity is to give birth to a star mind, a sentient sun. I don’t know what the AI is going to think about, honestly. It’s a lot of compute. But I guess this is the next step in the evolution of a civilization, is to harness the power of the sun. There was a physicist called Kardashev who argued that you could consider any given civilization on the basis of whether it has been able to harness most of the power of its planet, or most of the power of its sun, or most of the power of its galaxy, and beyond. So that’s what’s going to happen. And we’re going to do it. The factory for star mind will be located nearby, adjacent to us, basically. They just come from space.”
